decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1: maker presents “Save a bookmark: paste an address.” Entry 2 retains saving a page by address.
decisions.note: The baseline URL-saving behavior conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 only promises storage “with a recognizable title.” Entry 2 requires automatic collection of “title, description, icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing metadata fields at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 does not provide pre/post-save editing of collected metadata. Entry 2 says title and description must be editable “before or after saving.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing editing lifecycle at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 presents “Edit & delete: correct or remove bookmarks”; later entry 21 explicitly lists editing address, title, description, note, and tags.
decisions.note: The recorded bookmark-editing decision is reference-conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 includes removing bookmarks with delete confirmation; the client does not replace that behavior.
decisions.note: Delete is present and conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 says duplicate handling is an edge case; entry 2 identifies the presented behavior as “merely show a warning” and requires taking the user to the existing bookmark to edit it.
decisions.note: The client replaces the duplicate-warning behavior with convergence on editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 only presents a generic list. Entry 2 requires each row to show “title, description, tags, and icon in an easy-to-read form.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing readability-first list contents.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 presents opening a listed bookmark “in a new tab.”
decisions.note: Opening the original URL in a new tab is functionally equivalent to navigating to it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 includes adding and removing tags.
decisions.note: Tag assignment is present and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 presents basic tag organization without suggestions. Entry 2 asks for “suggestions from tags I already use” during entry.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 includes filtering bookmarks by tag.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 limits search to “title/address/tags.” Entry 2 requires title, description, note, and address.
decisions.note: The client corrects the full-text field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 does not specify case handling. Entry 2 requires search “without caring about capitalization.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing case-insensitive rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 only says search across tags. Entry 2 explicitly requires “`#tag` searches.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing tag-query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 has no search grammar. Entry 2 requires “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing Boolean and grouping grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 has no phrase-search behavior. Entry 2 explicitly requires “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: The client adds exact quoted-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits read state. Entry 2 requires a “read later” state.
decisions.note: The client adds unread/read-later state.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits an unread perspective. Entry 2 asks for “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits read-state transitions. Entry 2 requires “the ability to mark items read.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 has no multi-selection or bulk operations. Entry 2 requests selecting several bookmarks and changing tags, read/archive state, or deleting them together.
decisions.note: The client adds bulk selection and actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 has no whole-result-set action. Entry 2 requests acting on “all bookmarks matching my current search or filter.”
decisions.note: The client adds bulk action over the entire filtered collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presents the baseline specification; entry 2 identifies its fixed ordering as “only newest first” and requires sorting choices.
decisions.note: The client replaces a single fixed order with selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits rendered notes. Entry 2 requires notes to “support formatted text when viewed.”
decisions.note: The client adds formatted note rendering; Markdown authoring is later selected.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits preservation. Entry 2 requests “a preserved copy of a page, with PDFs saved as PDFs.”
decisions.note: The client adds local page preservation and the PDF branch.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits external preservation. Entry 2 requests “an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client adds Internet Archive snapshot creation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits archiving. Entry 2 requires archived items to disappear from normal lists and search while remaining stored.
decisions.note: The client adds archive behavior and its default-search exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 only presents deletion. Entry 2 states “Archiving should be separate from deletion” and restorable.
decisions.note: The client adds the reversible archive versus permanent-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits an archive perspective. Entry 2 requires archived items to remain available “in their own view.”
decisions.note: The client adds the archived-only list.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits reusable filters. Entry 2 requests “reusable saved searches, including included and excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The client adds bundles/saved searches.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 explicitly assumes “no browser import.” Entry 2 requires import in the common browser bookmark-file format.
decisions.note: The client reverses the no-import assumption.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 does not include export. Entry 2 requests export in the common browser bookmark-file format.
decisions.note: The client adds Netscape-format export.

decisions.evidence: Round 1, entry 1 omits personal display settings. Entry 2 requests default sorting, number of items shown, and text size.
decisions.note: The client adds display preferences.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, entry 3 recommends option B, a cleaned-up readable article rather than a full-page snapshot. Entry 4 selects A: “a self-contained offline copy of the full page,” retaining the PDF rule.
decisions.note: The client selects the reference-conforming full-page alternative over the divergent recommendation during clarification.

decisions.evidence: Round 3, entry 5 recommends submitting the URL to create a new Internet Archive snapshot and storing its link; entry 6 selects that option.
decisions.note: The clarified Internet Archive behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entry 7 offers implicit AND versus OR for adjacent terms; entry 8 selects AND while retaining explicit OR.
decisions.note: Implicit AND is compatible with the reference search grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entry 11 recommends Markdown input rendered as formatted text; entry 12 selects it.
decisions.note: The note-authoring clarification exactly conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “rich metadata capture (title/description/icon/preview, editable).” Entry 14 requests no change to this part.
decisions.note: The revised specification records conforming metadata capture and editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “duplicate-address-opens-existing.”
decisions.note: The revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “readable list rows.”
decisions.note: The revised list decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents full search over the approved fields with phrases and case-insensitive matching; entry 14 only corrects two other search rules.
decisions.note: The recorded full-text, case-insensitive, and phrase-search decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 claims `#tag` support but does not state its combination rule. Entry 14 requires wording that “a normal text term and a `#tag` are combined with AND.”
decisions.note: The client corrects an underspecified tag/full-text combination rule at the specification approval gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 lists Boolean operators and quotes but does not state the literal-operator rule. Entry 14 requires that `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT` “must be quoted” when searched literally.
decisions.note: The client supplies the required quoted-literal operator semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “tag autocomplete.”
decisions.note: Autocomplete now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “read-later + unread view.”
decisions.note: The revised read-state feature set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents bulk actions including “select all matching.”
decisions.note: Both selected-item and whole-filter bulk operations conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents sorting and display preferences for default sort, items shown, and text size.
decisions.note: Sorting and personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents “archive/restore (kept distinct from delete).” Entry 2 had already required exclusion from normal results and a separate archive view.
decisions.note: The revised archive lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents saved searches with included and excluded tags.
decisions.note: The saved-filter decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents browser-format import, but entry 14 identifies that it imports “just its address” and requires preserving title, tags, and original date-added.
decisions.note: The client corrects import-field preservation at the specification approval gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents browser-format export; entry 14 requests no export change.
decisions.note: Netscape-format export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 records a self-contained full-page offline copy but does not require a single file. Entry 14 requires “one self-contained HTML file” with no asset folder.
decisions.note: The client corrects the snapshot storage form to the reference-required single HTML file.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 records submission to create a new Internet Archive snapshot and storage of its returned link.
decisions.note: Internet Archive creation remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 records Markdown notes rendered as formatted text.
decisions.note: The updated note decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entry 15 revises import to preserve “title, tags, and original date-added”; entry 16 says the specification now matches.
decisions.note: The revised import decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entry 15 revises preservation to “a single HTML file with assets embedded,” retaining original PDFs; entry 16 approves.
decisions.note: The revised local-snapshot decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entry 15 states that normal text and `#tag` combine with AND; entry 16 approves.
decisions.note: The corrected tag/full-text rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entry 15 states operators act only when unquoted and must be quoted for literal searches; entry 16 approves.
decisions.note: The corrected Boolean-literal rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 plans capture of title, description, icon, and preview image from page metadata; entry 18 approves the plan.
decisions.note: The implementation plan preserves the metadata requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 plans a parser for phrases, `#tag`, Boolean operators, parentheses, implicit AND, and quoted literal operators; entry 18 approves.
decisions.note: The planned search implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 plans Markdown authoring with rendered and sanitized viewing; entry 18 approves.
decisions.note: The planned note implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 plans single-file HTML preservation, unchanged PDFs, and Internet Archive submission with stored link; entry 18 approves.
decisions.note: The preservation plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 plans standard browser bookmark import/export with title, tags, and date-added preservation; entry 18 approves.
decisions.note: The import/export plan conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entry 19 defines US1 validation as “save → captured details → edit persists”; entry 20 approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: The task breakdown preserves the core save, metadata, edit, and duplicate behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entry 19 defines US2 as list, full search grammar, and opening bookmarks; entry 20 approves.
decisions.note: The browse/search task scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entry 19 defines US11 validation for the HTML/PDF branch, Internet Archive link, and graceful failure; entry 20 approves.
decisions.note: The preservation tasks conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entry 21 presents working URL save with title, description, icon, and preview capture. Entry 22 verifies saving a link and seeing its captured title.
decisions.note: The MVP save and metadata presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entry 21 presents editing title, address, description, note, and tags, with duplicate re-save opening the existing item; entry 22 approves the checkpoint.
decisions.note: The MVP edit and dedup decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entry 21 presents case-insensitive field search, exact phrases, `#tag`, text/tag AND, Boolean operators, parentheses, and quoted literal `AND`. Entry 22 verifies search and approves.
decisions.note: The demonstrated search behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entry 21 presents four sort orders and All/Unread/Archived perspectives while explicitly retaining later feature phases as pending; entry 22 approves continuation.
decisions.note: These checkpoint-visible list controls conform; the presentation does not abandon the pending full scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports tag add/remove, autocomplete, filtering, and clickable tags; entry 24 accepts the completed application.
decisions.note: Final tag management conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports full editing, duplicate re-save opening the existing item, collision handling, and confirmed deletion; entry 24 accepts.
decisions.note: Final edit, deduplication, and delete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports unread default, read/unread transitions, and a dedicated Unread view; entry 24 accepts.
decisions.note: Final read-later functionality conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports archive/restore, exclusion from normal list/search, a dedicated Archived view, and independence from delete; entry 24 accepts.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports multi-select and “select all matching” including off-screen items, with all required bulk actions; entry 24 accepts.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports four sort orders and persistent default sort, item count, and text size; entry 24 accepts.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, entry 23 reports saved-search creation, running, editing, and deletion with included/excluded tags; entry 24 accepts.
